newsitem.title: JAPAN: High stocks seen depressing Japan gas oil imports.
newsitem.headline: High stocks seen depressing Japan gas oil imports.

text.p: Japan's spot gas oil imports, which usually pick up towards the spring, are expected to remain slack this year due to ample domestic inventories, middle distillates traders said on Wednesday.
Japan tends to import more gas oil in the spring as many refineries are closed for routine maintenance checks in the period.
Gas oil imports in the three-month period from April to June 1996 accounted for about 46 percent of Japan's total imports in the year.
This year, however, gas oil importers have kept a low profile and are likely to remain that way well into the three-month spring turnaround period amid plentiful stocks, traders said.
Japan's gas oil stockpiles at the end of January, the latest period for which data is available, totalled 2.4 million kilolitres (kl), up 25 percent from a year earlier.

Meanwhile, high kerosene stocks are unlikely to have as much impact on Japan's kerosene buying patterns as gas oil stocks have on gas oil imports, as kerosene imports taper off towards the spring anyway, traders said.
Japan's kerosene stocks at the end of January jumped 30 percent from a year earlier to 3.4 million kl.
